Wizard Viperian's Focus ability disrupts spellcasters more than expected - it imposes disadvantage on all.

GMs: Use Focus when players cluster; their failure to spread out is your opportunity to disrupt their spellcasting.

One ruling a day, no fluff. Follow @bizzalgames70.

Movement often surprises players with its flexibility - climbing, crawling, jumping.

DMs: Enforce the same climbing, crawling, and jumping rules for both players and monsters to avoid the usual disputes.

Save this for your next session. Daily rulings: @bizzalgames70

Judge's call: Elf.

Judges: Drill them on using the d20 action die for melee and spellcasting each turn until it's second nature.

Bookmark it before your players find the loophole. @bizzalgames70

In the dark, Cursed Knight of St. Ydris matters.

Players: Use Demonic Possession early, then switch to witch spells when the enemy's defenses crumple - stop leaning on luck.

Send this to the rules-lawyer in your group. @bizzalgames70

Major Image shifts the action economy more than players expect - it can remove a turn entirely.

DMs: Use Major Image to create a 20-foot cube illusion that forces enemy casters to waste actions on Investigation checks.

Ran it differently at your table? Drop it in the comments. @bizzalgames70

Itinerant Grasper tests the table's priorities.

Judges: When the spellcasters get too comfortable, introduce the Itinerant Grasper's 50% magic resistance to remind them of their hubris.

Daily tabletop RPG rulings. Follow @bizzalgames70 for one a day.

Control Water shapes entire lakes - 100 feet wide and deep.

GMs: Use Control Water's 100-foot reach to flood a passage, forcing them to rethink their route or drown.

Ran it differently at your table? Drop it in the comments. @bizzalgames70

Harpy's Luring Song catches parties off guard - Wisdom save DC 11 is deceptively low.

DMs: Use a Silence spell to nullify the Harpy's Luring Song and force it into melee, exploiting its low AC of 11.

Ran it differently at your table? Drop it in the comments. @bizzalgames70

Throwing Blade's return feature catches players off guard - it always flies back to the wielder's hand after.

Judges: Identify one obstacle this session where Throwing Blade's 20-foot range solves a problem without swinging swords.

Save this for your next session. Daily rulings: @bizzalgames70

GMs: Hand the fighter an eleventh sword and watch them struggle with disadvantage on their next climb check.

Clockwork Soul's spell list is deceptively robust - always prepared, never a wasted slot.

DMs: Stick to Clockwork Magic's always-prepared spells like dispel magic; flashy spells won't save you from dead levels.

Patron Bond and Invoke Patron can rewrite a wizard's personality - patron taint accumulates with each bond.

Judges: Enforce patron taint accumulation with each bond to remind players that their wizards' personalities are at stake.
